newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks seen up after employment data.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks seen up after employment data.

text.p: Wall Street was seen seen opening higher on Tuesday after the fourth-quarter employment cost index came in lower than expected, analysts said.
Peter Cardillo, Director of Research at Westfalia Investements, said: "It's basically what the Street was expecting. We came in less that one percent and that's good.
"Bonds are strong so the (stock) market will have a strong opening. I think we'll stablize today and move higher."

"The data tell us that we have had higher wages. That shouldn't scare anyone. It shows the economy is moving ahead. Inflation is not getting out of hand and does not pose a threat of accelerating. That is the key."

The fourth quarter ECI rose 0.8 percent, after rising 0.6 percent in the third quarter, the Labor Department said. Economists polled by Reuters estimated, on average, that the ECI would rise 0.9 percent in the fourth quarter.
